sourceChecks.title: Bacterial Viability in Self-Healing Concrete: A Case Study of Non-Ureolytic Bacillus Species
sourceChecks.excerpt: Cracks with a width of about 0.13 mm were filled with bacterial calcium carbonate within 14 to 28 days
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In cementitious composites, bacterial calcium carbonate filled cracks about 0.13 mm wide within 14–28 days; larger cracks were not entirely healed.

sourceChecks.title: Service Life Prediction Based on Sorptivity for Highway Concrete Exposed to Sulfate Attack and Freeze-Thaw Conditions
sourceChecks.excerpt: estimating the service life of concrete pavements and bridge decks exposed to sulfate attack and freeze-thaw deterioration
sourceChecks.paraphrase: NIST describes CONCLIFE, a model using concrete and environmental inputs to estimate spalling under sulfate attack and freeze-thaw.
sourceChecks.limitations: Only two deterioration mechanisms and a specified service-life tool; does not establish universal centuries-long forecasts or <5% error.

sourceChecks.title: Bond-Slip Behavior between Stainless Steel Rebars and Concrete

sourceChecks.paraphrase: Experimental reinforced-concrete specimens showed stainless-steel rebar bond behavior comparable to carbon steel; the paper describes stainless steel as more corrosion-resistant.
sourceChecks.limitations: Does not demonstrate thermodynamic/kinetic immunity in all exposures, low cost at scale, stray-current immunity, or universal infrastructure savings.

sourceChecks.limitations: This is frequency-specific structural modeling and reports further testing is needed; it does not demonstrate real-time reversible adaptation or response across hazards.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: metamaterial structural frame adaptive stiffness damping seismic beam column connection primary study
